data_points.source_name: Market.us (Sunscreen industry statistics, citing Statista/ProdegeMR Feb-2019 survey)
data_points.notes: 32.77% of surveyed Indian respondents used sun care products daily (Feb-2019 ProdegeMR survey via Statista, relayed by Market.us); 25.62% never use; 14.61% more than twice weekly. Survey respondents, not population-weighted penetration.

India sunscreen market USD 576.6mn 2025, forecast USD 996.0mn by 2034. Effectively identical to the IMARC USD 0.577bn 2025 SEGMENT-level sun_care figure already on file - i.e. IMARC's 'sun care' number on file is actually its sunscreen sizing. CONFLICTS with TechSci USD 893.12mn 2024 and with IMARC's own broader sun care products sizing of USD 1.4bn 2025 (2.4x). Aggregator; organised/unorganised coverage not stated.
India sunscreen CAGR 6.07% 2026-2034 (USD 576.6mn 2025 to USD 996.0mn 2034). Close to TechSci 6.8% 2025-2030 despite a large base-size disagreement.

India sunscreen market USD 893.12mn 2024, forecast USD 1,325.37mn by 2030. Identical to the TechSci USD 0.893bn 2024 SEGMENT-level sun_care figure already on file - i.e. that on-file segment figure is actually TechSci's sunscreen sizing. CONFLICTS with IMARC USD 576.6mn 2025 (1.5x gap). Aggregator; organised/unorganised coverage not stated.
India sunscreen CAGR 6.8% 2025-2030 (USD 893.12mn 2024 to USD 1,325.37mn 2030). Close to IMARC 6.07% despite base-size disagreement.

India sun care PRODUCTS market USD 1.4bn 2025, forecast USD 2.2bn by 2034. IMARC's broader sun-care scope: 2.4x its own India sunscreen sizing (USD 576.6mn 2025) - scope likely adds after-sun/tanning plus SPF-adjacent products, definition not disclosed. Segment-level spread across aggregators now USD 162mn (MarkNtel) to USD 1.4bn (IMARC) for 2025: >20% gap, do NOT publish a reconciled segment size.
India sun care products CAGR 5.05% 2026-2034 (USD 1.4bn 2025 to USD 2.2bn 2034).

India sun care market USD 162mn 2025, USD 195mn 2026, USD 395mn 2032. EXTREME outlier at the low end: 8.6x below IMARC's USD 1.4bn and 3.6x below IMARC sunscreen-only. Likely organised/urban-only or narrower category definition (undisclosed). Documents the aggregator spread; unusable for reconciliation.
India sun care CAGR 12.48% 2026-2032. Highest growth estimate on file for the segment (vs IMARC 5.05%, TechSci 6.8%, IMARC sunscreen 6.07%) - from the smallest base.

data_points.methodology: Sample = Nykaa written reviews for Nykaa SKUs listing inside Rs1,500-3,000 MRP in the Phase 1 sweep, restricted to the two hero formats (sunscreen, pigmentation/brightening serum) plus Korean moisturisers and toners/essences. Two frames, never pooled: every retrievable 1- and 2-star review ('negative'), and the first 3 pages of Nykaa's default 'most useful' ordering, which is overwhelmingly 5-star. Themes are regex-matched then polarity-checked against a negation window, so 'no white cast' counts as NEGATED (the product lacks the problem) and never as a complaint. A review is the unit of observation: these are statistics about REVIEWS, not about users or buyers. Every review and URL is in data/raw/premium_skin_reviews_20260810T022519Z.json.
